topSignals.title: Ceres Power's H1 2026 results reveal the first disclosed SOFC stack-supply contract value in this monitor and a fresh data-center TAM framing.
topSignals.text: Reporting before today's UK open (Sept 23), Ceres posted revenue up 8% to £22.8M, an adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to £6.8M, and cash of £172M after a £102.6M oversubscribed equity raise. On the earnings call CEO Phil Caldwell disclosed that manufacturing licensee Doosan has secured its first export order — roughly £60M in stack supplies — to Reverion in Germany, that licensee Weichai (China) is targeting 200 MW of capacity within two years after completing full technology transfer, and that data centers now represent ~50% of Ceres's estimated 22 GW total addressable market by 2030. Caldwell also cited NVIDIA's estimate that 800V DC-direct architecture saves ~5% of the AC/DC conversion loss in a data center, becoming a likely requirement around 2028-2029 — the same efficiency argument Bloom has been making for its own DC-native SOFC delivery. Investing.com transcript | ADVFN

topSignals.title: Germany's EEG-Novelle 2027 and accompanying Netzpaket get their first Bundestag reading tonight, Sept 24, 20:35 CET
topSignals.text: (25 minutes allotted per item, live-streamed). Coverage ahead of the debate focuses on a controversial Economics Ministry plan to eventually eliminate fixed feed-in tariffs for small PV (≤25 kW) and require mandatory direct marketing — drawing coalition pushback — but reporting reviewed today gives no explicit detail yet on how the reform treats larger self-generation/behind-the-meter installations (the category relevant to SOFC data-center power) beyond referral to committee after this reading, targeting Jan 1, 2027 entry into force. Worth checking tomorrow's monitor run for outcome and committee assignment. pv magazine | Bundestag

topSignals.title: Priority stacks: Elcogen breaks its quiet streak with a whitepaper, not a commercial announcement; Topsoe logs an eighth consecutive quiet day.
topSignals.text: Elcogen published "The Case for Solid Oxide Electrolysis Technology" on Sept 23 — an SOEC/green-hydrogen positioning piece, not a new SOFC or data-center development; standing status otherwise unchanged since the Sept 21 Metrosert testing-cooperation deal. Direct checks of topsoe.com confirm no new release since the Sept 7 Uniper e-methanol FEED contract. Elcogen News&Insights | Topsoe Press Releases

items.text: Elcogen (priority): New but off-topic for SOFC/data-center purposes — see Top Signal #3 (SOEC whitepaper, Sept 23). Standing status otherwise unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform, ELCO I Tallinn factory ramping toward 360 MW/yr, Metrosert testing cooperation (Sept 21).

Topsoe (priority): No new news — eighth consecutive quiet day (Top Signal #3). SOEC-only Herning factory (500 MW/yr) remains the flagship asset; SOFC/data-center pathway still deferred under the May 2026 roadmap review.

Ceres Power: H1 2026 results and earnings-call disclosures — see Top Signal #1 (Doosan's first export order to Reverion, ~£60M stack supplies; Weichai targeting 200 MW capacity within two years; data centers ~50% of Ceres's 22 GW TAM). Company reiterated guidance of signing roughly one new manufacturing licensee per year on average.
No new stack/cell announcements found from Bloom Energy, FuelCell Energy, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, or Aisin in the last 24-48h.

Top story — see Top Signal #2:* Germany's EEG-Novelle 2027 and Netzpaket receive their first Bundestag reading tonight (Sept 24, 20:35 CET). Standing background unchanged: both US federal large-load cost-shift bills (Ratepayer Protection Act, GRID Savings Act) remain dead after the Sept 17 dual-block; Trump-Thune conversations on a companion bill continue with no text yet; Sen. Van Hollen's "Power for the People Act" (S.3682) and Sen. Wyden's data-center excise-tax white paper remain pending; PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement bid window opens Sept 30 (through Oct 21); FERC RM26-4 Section 206 show-cause responses due Nov 16; Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; US ITC 48E 30% fuel-cell credit (natural-gas/biogas SOFC qualifies post-OBBBA, domestic-content thresholds 45%/50%/55% in 2026-28); New York's permit moratorium; Texas's development pause; EPA turbine NSPS "temporary" classification (in force since Jan 15, 2026, under legal challenge).

Bloom Energy (BE): Closed Sept 23 at $275.19 (-0.48%); market cap ~$81.1B (+308% YTD). Analyst consensus "Buy" (29 analysts), average price target $280.24. Securities class-action (scandium-sourcing allegations) lead-plaintiff deadline Sept 28; Q3 earnings Oct 27. No new operational news — recurring "record Q2 2026" guidance coverage in German-language finance media (ad-hoc-news.de) is a rehash of the July 28 Q2 print, not new.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Closed Sept 23 at $17.18 (-3.81%). No new operational disclosures; continued wave of plaintiff-firm reminder press releases (Kaplan Fox, others) for the Nov 10, 2026 lead-plaintiff deadline over the Fit Energy cost-overrun disclosure. Backlog remains $3.6B per the Q3 transcript.

Ceres Power (CWR.L): H1 2026 results out — see Top Signal #1. Revenue +8% to £22.8M, adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to £6.8M, cash £172M post-raise. Market commentary (AskTraders) noted shares fell despite the narrower loss and cash boost, suggesting the market focused on compressed gross margin (71%, down from 79%, on a shift to lower-margin hardware/engineering work) over the headline improvement.

lcoe.text: Cross-validated DC-delivery efficiency claim: Ceres's H1 call cites NVIDIA's estimate that 800V DC-direct data-center architecture saves ~5% of AC/DC conversion loss, becoming a likely requirement ~2028-2029 — this is now the second SOFC vendor (after Bloom's own capex/TCO claims, carried forward from Sept 17) making the same efficiency argument, strengthening the case for weighting DC-delivery efficiency gains in the model rather than treating it as one vendor's marketing claim.

First disclosed stack-supply contract value from a Ceres licensee: Doosan's export order to Reverion (Germany) is reported at ~£60M for stack supplies, but MW capacity is not disclosed — insufficient alone to derive a $/kW benchmark; flagged for follow-up if MW figures surface.
Market-sizing datapoint, not a cost figure: Ceres frames data centers as ~50% of its ~22 GW total addressable market by 2030 — useful context for the model's demand-side assumptions.

Carry-forward, unchanged: Henry Hub EIA full-year 2026 average estimate ~$3.43-3.44/MMBtu (August STEO), still below the model's carried $4.00-4.30/MMBtu assumption — worth reconciling; US ITC 48E 30% credit for natural-gas/biogas SOFC; Virginia's $0.011/kWh self-generation tax; PJM's $555/MW-day backstop ceiling.

Pending calendar: Germany EEG-Novelle first Bundestag reading (today, Sept 24, 20:35 CET), Bloom lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), PJM backstop bid window (Sept 30-Oct 21), Bloom Q3 earnings (Oct 27), FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline (Nov 10).
